 At Indore

sentences.text: Before
Hon'Ble
Shri Justice
Subodh Abhyankar

On The 3 rd Of September, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 38537 of 2025
 Ramprakash
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Dharmendra Chelawat - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Vishal Singh Panwar- G.A. for the State.
 Shri Sandeep Yadav- Advocate for the objector.
 Order
1] They are heard.
Perused the case-diary.

2] This is the first application (although wrong application as second application) filed by the applicant under Section 482 of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023/Section 438 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 for grant of anticipatory bail as he is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.189/2025 registered at Police Station Mahila Thana, District Indore for the offence punishable under Sections 294, 323, 376, 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
3] Allegation against the applicant is of rape on the pretext of marriage.
4] Counsel for the applicant has submitted that admittedly, the FIR has been lodged on 11.08.2025, whereas, the incident is said to have taken place between 11.05.2014 to 11.07.2022.

Counsel has submitted that it is not denied that the prosecutrix was a consenting party, as she has resided with the applicant for a period of around eight years, and only because of a dispute between them, the FIR
NEUTRAL
CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:24885 2 MCRC-38537-2025 has been lodged.
It is also submitted that the prosecutrix was already married to some other person, and was having a dispute with her husband.

So far as the allegations regarding obtaining loan is concerned, it is submitted that a house was purchased in the joint name of the applicant and the prosecutrix for a consideration of Rs.29 Lakhs,

1 in which, she contributed Rs.6 Lakhs and a loan of Rs.24 Lakhs was also obtained, which was in the name of the applicant only, and he is also paying the installments.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The documents regarding the payment of the installments have also been filed on record.
It is further submitted that the prosecutrix had also executed an affidavit in favour of the applicant that she would reside with him unconditionally.
Thus, it is submitted that the custodial interrogation of the applicant in such circumstances would not be necessary.

5] Counsel for the objector/prosecutrix, on the other hand, has vehemently opposed the prayer, and it is submitted that looking to the allegations levelled against the applicant, no case for grant of bail is made out, especially when he has also duped the complainant.
6] The prosecutrix has also appeared through V.C. to oppose the prayer.

7] Having considered the rival submissions, on perusal of the case-diary, as also the documents filed on record, it is found that the FIR in the present case was lodged on 11.08.2025, whereas, the date of incident is stated to be from 11.05.2014 to 11.07.2022.

Thus, it is apparent that the FIR has been lodged after around eleven years from the initial date of incident, and after three years from the last date of incident, and there is no explanation regarding delay in lodging the FIR.

It is also found that the prosecutrix had also executed an affidavit in favour of the applicant that she would reside with him unconditionally, and it is also found that the loan documents have also been filed on record to demonstrate that the applicant was also paying the installments of the loan.
In such circumstances, this Court is of the considered opinion that his custodial interrogation would not be necessary.
8] Accordingly, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:24885 3 MCRC-38537-2025 application is allowed.

It is directed that in the event of arrest, applicant shall be released on bail, upon his executing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/-
(Rupees Twenty Five Thousand only) and furnishing one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer (Investigating Officer).
The applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a Police Officer, as and when required.

He shall further abide by the other conditions enumerated in Sub Section (2) of Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973.
9] Accordingly, MCRC stands allowed and disposed of.
Certified copy as per rules.
